name: International Maritime Boundaries of India (IMBL & Maritime Treaties)
description: Bilateral and UNCLOS international maritime boundary lines separating the Indian Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and territorial waters from neighboring sovereign nations: Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Maldives, Myanmar, Indonesia, and Thailand.

properties.name: India–Sri Lanka Maritime Boundary (IMBL)
properties.sector: Palk Strait & Gulf of Mannar Sector
properties.description: Demarcated border between Tamil Nadu (India) and Northern / North-Western Province (Sri Lanka). Crossing is strictly prohibited for Indian artisanal fishers; high risk of boat seizure by Sri Lankan Navy. Maintain at least a 5 km safe buffer zone.

properties.name: India–Pakistan Maritime Boundary
properties.sector: Sir Creek / Kutch Arabian Sea Sector
properties.description: Demarcated maritime boundary in the Arabian Sea off the coast of Gujarat (Kutch/Kathiawar) and Sindh. Indian trawlers and fishers from Okha, Porbandar, and Veraval must NOT cross north-west into Pakistani waters; immediate risk of arrest by Pakistan Maritime Security Agency (PMSA). Maintain 5 km clearance.

properties.name: India–Bangladesh Maritime Boundary
properties.sector: Sundarbans / Northern Bay of Bengal Sector
properties.treaty: 2014 UN PCA ITLOS Maritime Delimitation Award
properties.description: Demarcated by the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) starting at the mouth of the Hariabhanga River in the Sundarbans and extending southward into the Bay of Bengal along 180° bearing. West Bengal and Odisha fishing boats must remain west of this line.

properties.name: India–Maldives Maritime Boundary
properties.description: Delimitation line running east-west along the Eight Degree Channel (approx Lat 7.68°N) separating Minicoy Island (Lakshadweep, India) from Ihavandhippolhu Atoll (Maldives). Indian vessels must remain north of this line.

properties.name: India–Myanmar Maritime Boundary
properties.description: Demarcated border through the Coco Channel (approx Lat 13.85°N) separating Landfall Island (North Andaman, India) from the Coco Islands (Myanmar), extending into the Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea. Indian vessels must remain south of this boundary.

properties.name: India–Indonesia Maritime Boundary
properties.sector: Great Channel / Six Degree Channel Sector
properties.description: Delimitation line along the Great Channel (Six Degree Channel) separating Indira Point (Great Nicobar Island, India) from Rondo Island and Aceh (Sumatra, Indonesia). Indian boats must remain north-west of this boundary.

properties.name: India–Thailand Maritime Boundary
properties.sector: Central Andaman Sea / Phuket Basin Sector
properties.description: Continental shelf seabed boundary in the Andaman Sea between India's Andaman & Nicobar EEZ and Thailand's continental shelf. Indian vessels must maintain clearance to the west.
